Decoding gene regulation in the immune system.

We combine high-throughput biophysical and functional studies with genomic data to understand how transcription factors coordinate immune-cell responses.

Our approach

From molecular interactions to systems-level insight

Immune cells must respond precisely to pathogens and signaling molecules. We study the signal-activated and cell-state transcription factors that coordinate these responses, linking biophysical mechanisms to genome-scale behavior in healthy and disease states.

Research themes

How we investigate immune gene regulation

01

TF specificity

We examine how closely related interferon regulatory factors and nuclear receptors recognize DNA and regulate distinct target genes.

02

Immune cell state

We study how lineage and polarization factors shape enhancer landscapes and cell-specific responses in monocytes and macrophages.

03

Technology development

We develop protein-binding microarray and functional genomic approaches to characterize TF binding, cooperativity, and allostery.
